content.text: I found a strong candidate: PR #1349 merged on September 6, added “Block props migrated v2,” and made the new settings store the default after migration. The key detail is that the store switch is shared across the graph, while personal settings migrate one user at a time. I’m checking how an older build behaves when another user flips that shared switch.

The code supports a specific failure mode: once the graph switches to block props, an older client can stop showing personal sections that still exist in the visible settings tree, because it now reads the separate props copy.

The new PR adds a per-user safeguard, but older builds do not have it. I’m also checking the initial migration for a way that props copy could have been left empty. So far, this is a code-supported hypothesis; I haven’t inspected the affected graph.

content.text:
The local reproduction confirmed the mechanism in the released code: with one personal section in the legacy tree and empty personal props, switching the shared flag on changes the sidebar’s section count from one to zero. If the old personal migration marker is already set, reloading skips the copy again.

That establishes a real failure path, though the affected graph still needs to show that data mismatch. I’ve prepared a read-only console check that compares section counts, flags, and marker dates without changing settings.

**I found a credible DG-side explanation that fits the timing and your old version:** a newer client may have switched the shared graph to reading block props, while users on your released version continued with empty or stale personal props. Their sidebar sections could still exist in the visible settings tree but no longer be the copy the extension displays.

I verified that failure path locally using the released source. **I haven’t confirmed that your graph has this data mismatch**, so this is a strong hypothesis rather than a diagnosed root cause. I’m interpreting “personal left sidebar” as the DG personal sections.

The version detail is particularly useful. `078990e8` is a commit in **Roam’s extension catalogue**, and its metadata points to DG source commit `35ac77ee`. It was released on August 24 as 0.22.0. Your build therefore predates the change that creates “Block props migrated v2.” [Your release’s catalogue entry](https://github.com/Roam-Research/roam-depot/blob/078990e81e75bbd994aeb7f9bbcd9c10afd3b555/extensions/DiscourseGraphs/discourse-graph.json)

Here is the system, starting from the sidebar you see.

Your personal sidebar is built from settings stored in the Roam graph. Originally, those settings lived in an ordinary, visible block tree:

```text
roam/js/discourse-graph
└── Left Sidebar
    ├── Global-Section
    │   └── Children
    │       └── shared sidebar items
    └── <your Roam user UID>/Personal-Section
        └── My research
            ├── Settings
            │   └── folding, aliases, limits…
            └── Children
                └── your sidebar items
```

The extension gets the current Roam user’s UID and finds the matching `<UID>/Personal-Section` block. “Personal” means selected for that user; the configuration still lives in the shared graph. [Personal-section lookup](https://github.com/DiscourseGraphs/discourse-graph/blob/35ac77ee/apps/roam/src/utils/getLeftSidebarSettings.ts#L156)

We then introduced another representation on the **same settings page**:

```text
roam/js/discourse-graph
├── Feature Flags
│   └── block props: shared feature switches
├── Global
│   └── block props: shared settings, including global sidebar items
└── <your Roam user UID>
    └── block props:
        "Left sidebar": [
          { name: "My research", Settings: {...}, Children: [...] }
        ]
```

“Block props” are structured data attached to a block. They are separate from the visible child bullets. Consequently, the visible legacy tree can contain your sections while the props attached to your UID block contain an empty list. [Settings-block layout](https://github.com/DiscourseGraphs/discourse-graph/blob/35ac77ee/apps/roam/src/components/settings/utils/zodSchema.ts#L276), [personal sidebar schema](https://github.com/DiscourseGraphs/discourse-graph/blob/35ac77ee/apps/roam/src/components/settings/utils/zodSchema.ts#L201)

**The migration copies the data; a separate flag decides which copy the application reads.** That distinction explains most of the confusing behavior here.

The original migration landed in [ENG-1519 / PR #876](https://github.com/DiscourseGraphs/discourse-graph/pull/876), merged March 13. On initialization, it copies shared settings into props and separately copies the **current user’s** personal settings. It records completion in two different places:

| Marker or flag | Where it lives | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `Block props migrated` | Visible block on the settings page | The original shared-settings migration recorded completion. |
| `dg-personal-settings-migrated` | Per-user extension settings | The original migration recorded completion for this user. |
| `Use new settings store` | Props on `Feature Flags` | Chooses legacy settings versus props for reads. |
| `Block props migrated v2` | Visible block on the settings page | The newer shared-settings migration recorded completion. |
| `dg-personal-settings-migrated-v2` | Per-user extension settings | The newer migration recorded completion for this user. |

The **graph marker does not mean every user’s personal settings were migrated**. The shared migration covers feature flags, global settings, and discourse-node configuration; personal migration is a separate operation. [Original migration](https://github.com/DiscourseGraphs/discourse-graph/blob/35ac77ee/apps/roam/src/components/settings/utils/migrateLegacyToBlockProps.ts#L173), [v2 personal migration](https://github.com/DiscourseGraphs/discourse-graph/blob/8a6d5379/apps/roam/src/components/settings/utils/migrateLegacyToBlockProps.ts#L292)

During the transition, DG’s sidebar settings UI writes to both representations. For example, adding a section creates legacy blocks and then synchronizes the section list into props. This is synchronization performed by the UI’s code; it is not a general guarantee that any manual edit to the visible settings tree updates props. [Section creation and synchronization](https://github.com/DiscourseGraphs/discourse-graph/blob/35ac77ee/apps/roam/src/components/settings/LeftSidebarPersonalSettings.tsx#L743)

The decisive recent change is **[ENG-2173 / PR #1349 — Enable props-based settings by default](https://github.com/DiscourseGraphs/discourse-graph/pull/1349)**. It merged September 6 at 21:22 UTC—September 7 in India—just before your September 8 observation.

Its startup sequence is:

1. Create missing settings blocks and **wait** for default-value writes.
2. Rerun the shared migration using the new `Block props migrated v2` marker.
3. Rerun the current user’s migration using `dg-personal-settings-migrated-v2`.
4. If both succeed, set the shared `Use new settings store` flag to `true`.
5. Also record `Props settings default migrated: true`, so a later admin rollback to legacy reads stays off across reloads.

The new markers force another migration pass even where the original markers already exist. Existing props can be overwritten with the parsed legacy values when they differ. On later loads, the markers cause those migration passes to be skipped. [Startup sequence](https://github.com/DiscourseGraphs/discourse-graph/blob/8a6d5379/apps/roam/src/components/settings/utils/init.ts#L390), [default-store switch](https://github.com/DiscourseGraphs/discourse-graph/blob/8a6d5379/apps/roam/src/components/settings/utils/migratePropsStoreDefault.ts#L27)

There was a concrete reason to revisit the original migration: **the original code recorded success without waiting for the props write to finish**. The older completion marker therefore was not proof that the copy had saved successfully. The v2 change waits for those writes and reports failures before marking completion. [Original write behavior](https://github.com/DiscourseGraphs/discourse-graph/blob/35ac77ee/apps/roam/src/components/settings/utils/migrateLegacyToBlockProps.ts#L102), [awaited v2 write](https://github.com/DiscourseGraphs/discourse-graph/blob/8a6d5379/apps/roam/src/components/settings/utils/migrateLegacyToBlockProps.ts#L102)

Now connect that to your situation:

1. You and other users run the August release.
2. Someone opens this shared graph using a newer main, beta, PR, or development build containing #1349.
3. Their client migrates shared settings and their own personal settings, creates the v2 marker, and enables the graph-wide props flag.
4. Your older client sees that flag and starts reading **your personal props**, even though it has not run the newer personal migration.
5. If your personal props are empty, your personal sidebar becomes empty.

Your released code has **no per-user readiness check before switching to props**. The new PR adds that safeguard, allowing newer clients to keep reading a user’s legacy settings until their v2 migration succeeds. It cannot add that safeguard to clients still running the old release. [Released reader](https://github.com/DiscourseGraphs/discourse-graph/blob/35ac77ee/apps/roam/src/components/settings/utils/accessors.ts#L895), [new readiness check](https://github.com/DiscourseGraphs/discourse-graph/blob/8a6d5379/apps/roam/src/components/settings/utils/accessors.ts#L911)

There is also no automatic rescue from the legacy sidebar tree: the sidebar builds its section list from the selected settings values. With an empty props list, it produces zero sections despite populated legacy blocks. [Sidebar merge behavior](https://github.com/DiscourseGraphs/discourse-graph/blob/35ac77ee/apps/roam/src/utils/getLeftSidebarSettings.ts#L246)

**I reproduced that exact selection behavior locally:**

| Source and state | Legacy sections present | Sections passed to sidebar |
|---|---:|---:|
| Released 0.22.0, legacy reads selected, empty props | 1 | 1 |
| Released 0.22.0, props reads selected, empty props | 1 | **0** |
| Released 0.22.0, props reads selected, populated props | 1 | 1 |
| Newer code, props selected but user’s v2 migration incomplete | 1 | 1 |

I also confirmed that the released personal migration performs no copy when the old personal marker is already true. That explains how reloading can fail to repair the situation. This reproduction executes the source functions with mocked Roam data; it is not a live graph or browser reproduction. [Reproduction results](/tmp/dg-sidebar-investigation-2026-09-20/results.json)

Of the PRs around the onset, #1349 is the strongest candidate because it both creates your observed marker and changes the settings source. Two potentially misleading sidebar references are:

- [PR #1299 — Left sidebar](https://github.com/DiscourseGraphs/discourse-graph/pull/1299), merged August 31, changed website documentation and screenshots.
- [PR #1419 — Remove `migrateLeftSideBarSettings`](https://github.com/DiscourseGraphs/discourse-graph/pull/1419) is still open, so it did not enter through main.

What remains unproven is **why the props would be empty or wrong for all affected users**. The mixed-version explanation requires that mismatch; switching stores alone does not break correctly populated personal props. It also does not fully explain an affected user who successfully ran v2 with intact legacy settings.

The next discriminating observation is therefore small: compare each user’s legacy section count with their props section count, check the shared flag, and check when the v2 marker was created. I prepared a [read-only console inspection script](/tmp/dg-sidebar-investigation-2026-09-20/inspect-graph-read-only.js) for that. It also checks whether DG’s sidebar container mounted. It has been syntax-checked but not run in your graph.

**Your old version does not rule out a DG regression caused by another client changing shared graph settings.** The source gives us a specific mechanism to investigate before attributing this to Roam. I made no repository or graph changes.

**First, temporarily switch the graph back to reading the legacy settings and see whether the sidebar returns.** There is an existing rollback control for this.

1. Open **Discourse Graphs settings**.
2. Open **Admin**. If it isn’t visible, press **Ctrl + Shift + A** while the settings dialog is open—Control on Mac too. [Shortcut implementation](https://github.com/DiscourseGraphs/discourse-graph/blob/35ac77ee/apps/roam/src/components/settings/Settings.tsx#L126)
3. Find **Use new settings store** and note whether it is on.
4. **If it is on, turn it off**, then reload your graph. This makes DG read the legacy settings again. It applies to shared and personal settings across the graph, so one person changes the flag; other users then reload. [Rollback control](https://github.com/DiscourseGraphs/discourse-graph/blob/35ac77ee/apps/roam/src/components/settings/AdminPanel.tsx#L423), [settings reader](https://github.com/DiscourseGraphs/discourse-graph/blob/35ac77ee/apps/roam/src/components/settings/utils/accessors.ts#L897)

**Leave both “Block props migrated” blocks in place.** Deleting migration markers can trigger another copy from legacy settings into props; that is unnecessary for this rollback.

What happens next determines our next move:

- **The sidebar returns:** that strongly implicates the props-reading path. Leave the flag off while we compare the two copies and determine why the personal props are missing or incorrect. Recovery comes first; the permanent fix needs to handle users on different extension versions.
- **The flag was already off, or switching it off does not help:** the proposed store-switch explanation is insufficient. Run the [read-only inspection script](/tmp/dg-sidebar-investigation-2026-09-20/inspect-graph-read-only.js) in Roam’s developer console and paste its output here. It compares the stored section counts and checks whether the sidebar container exists, without changing graph data.

**Tell me whether the flag was on, and whether switching it off brings your personal sections back.**

**These logs show a working settings-to-sidebar path for your user. They also show that this startup did not restore the sidebar by rerunning migration.** The `dd` section was already present in props before migration, and all three migration steps were skipped.

Here is the path recorded in your logs:

| Stage | What it contains |
|---|---|
| Cached legacy settings | `dd`, with two children |
| Stored personal props | `dd`, with the same two children |
| Settings returned to the application | `dd` |
| Configuration passed to the sidebar | `dd` |
| Sidebar mounted | `rootPresent` changes from `false` to `true` |

All reported personal settings match the selected reader’s expected values. There are no missing props or schema-validation errors in this capture.

The mental model is: **migration copies settings; the store flag selects which copy to read; the sidebar renders that result.** On current main, personal props are selected when both `Use new settings store` and the current user’s v2 migration marker are true. Both are true here. The migration marker makes subsequent migration attempts skip; it does not continuously reconcile legacy settings with props. See the [reader selection](/mnt/data/projects/discourse-graph/apps/roam/src/components/settings/utils/accessors.ts:898) and [personal migration guard](/mnt/data/projects/discourse-graph/apps/roam/src/components/settings/utils/migrateLegacyToBlockProps.ts:292).

**The `ss`/`gg` discrepancy needs another measurement—and I found a limitation in my logger.** Its “live legacy” lookup selected the first `Left Sidebar` block returned by an unsorted pull. The application selects from a tree sorted by block order. If your settings page has multiple `Left Sidebar` blocks, those lookups can select different roots.

That means this warning:

> Live legacy sidebar differs from the cached tree used by the legacy reader.

does **not yet prove a stale cache**. It could be my diagnostic comparing two different branches of the settings page. Likewise, `differsFromLegacy: false` compares props against the cached `dd` copy; it does not establish agreement with the `ss`/`gg` copy.

My current assessment is:

- The earlier “empty personal props” hypothesis does **not describe your user in this capture**.
- A settings-source or block-selection problem remains plausible. We changed both the extension version and the store selection, so this successful load cannot isolate which change restored visibility.
- The v2 marker was created **September 7 at 4:02 p.m. IST**, which fits your reported onset. That establishes timing, not causation.
- Another user’s row still shows two legacy sections and zero props sections. We cannot call this fixed for everyone, and the corrected root lookup matters for interpreting that row too.

I’ve updated the diagnostic on `left-sidebar-debug` to report every matching sidebar root, its order, and its personal blocks. The rebuilt extension is ready in [apps/roam/dist](/mnt/data/projects/discourse-graph/apps/roam/dist). Roam type checking, all **533 unit tests**, the diagnostic lint checks, and the build passed.

Reload that local extension, then run this in the browser console to copy the smaller report we need:

```js
(() => {
  const r = JSON.parse(window.dgPersonalSettingsDebug());
  copy(JSON.stringify({
    selection: r.sidebar.selection,
    warnings: r.warnings,
    users: r.users
  }, null, 2));
})();
```

That will show whether `dd` and `ss`/`gg` sit beneath different roots, or whether the live and cached reads genuinely disagree about the same root. It gives us a concrete next step before choosing any settings repair.

```bash
cd /mnt/data/projects/discourse-graph

entire session attach 01a0bd6f-6c07-7d13-b7e4-c9a839e83ceb \
```

This creates a checkpoint and **amends the latest commit** to add its `Entire-Checkpoint` reference, changing the commit SHA.

Verify that the checkpoint is attached:

```bash
entire checkpoint explain HEAD --short
```
